author: jessica
_note: TESTCASE 02, A DIFFERENT LOST THING ON THE SAME FOUR BEATS. His go, 2026-10-02 21:03: "yeah lets try
abother artifact recipe". The question it answers: is carry-absence-recover-return a FAMILY or one
mission? So the template, the place rules and the leash are testcase 01's unchanged, and everything
the player reads is new: the object, the absence, the people waiting and why it matters to them.
Testcase 01 was a utility (water). This one is a comms relay, and the reason it matters is that the
people at the <Place> have not spoken to home since it went down. The last box pays that off.

place._theme: Testcase 01's delivery rule, unchanged on purpose: people who are waiting on the relay have to be there. LocTypeOE_NonHostile, pool 62 when measured 2026-09-24.
place._civilians: Off, as testcase 01: the site brings its own people.

prose.name: Hauling: Relay Dish on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The <Place> has been without a comms relay for over a week. The dish was signed out to them and never arrived, so I should find where it stopped.
prose._prose: Artifact family title shape, Category: thing on <Planet> (style guide 4b), as testcase 01. Journal lines follow section 3: first person, what just happened then what next, about 23 words, and beat 4 is the standalone recap.

items._items: Jessica's, 2026-10-02. Named objects, never a described site.
items._crateModel: Testcase 01's freight crate, his eye 2026-09-24: a consignment, not loot.
items._centre: PLACEHOLDER, Jessica's pick 2026-10-02 off `gen_inspect static Satellite`: a free-standing tripod dish (RadarDish01 and the CommRadarDish stack were the alternatives). Never seen in game as an activator; his eye decides whether it reads and sits right.

beats.journal: I found the dish crate, set down well short of the <Place>. The tag says the transmitter went ahead on its own. I should take the dish there.

message.title: Shipping Tag
message.text: SHIPPING TAG. To: <Place>. Relay dish, 1 of 2. Transmitter, 2 of 2, shipped separately. Handle with care. Somebody didn't.

beats.journal: The transmitter reached the <Place> and was taken from its crate before anyone could fit it. Without it the dish is just a dish. I need to find who took it.

message.title: Comms Log
message.text: COMMS LOG, <Place>. Relay down, nine days. Transmitter crate: arrived, opened, empty. Dish: still out there somewhere. Nobody here has spoken to home since.

beats.journal: I've got the transmitter back, still in its packing. I should take it to the <Place> and get the relay working.

message.title: Relay Transmitter
message.text: Relay Transmitter (2 of 2). Still in its packing. Someone has written a price on the box in grease pencil, and it isn't much.

beats.journal: A comms relay bound for the <Place> was shipped in two crates, and neither arrived whole. I found the dish, took the transmitter back from the thieves and brought the relay online.

message.title: Relay Online
message.text: Dish and transmitter fitted. The relay at the <Place> is live, and the first call out of it was somebody ringing home.

_messages: Texts and titles are Jessica's, 2026-10-02. Each box is a MESG cloned the same way as testcase 01's, so <Place> resolves.
_journal: Contractions on purpose (didn't, I've, isn't): the journal and the boxes are people writing in a hurry, and a log with none reads generated (the Outlaws 01 read, 2026-10-02).
